blocks.text: Among the more recent writers, אנקה anaka is, for Pagnino, who followed the Greeks and Jerome, the mygale; for Deodati the mus araneus [shrew-mouse]; for Münster and the Genevans the ericius [hedgehog], as if on the authority of Onkelos, whose Paraphrase is corrupt here; for Junius and Buxtorf the attelabus, as if on the authority of the Jerusalem translator, whom they had not sufficiently understood; for Castellio the fiber [beaver], on the authority of Rabbi Solomon; for Arias the viverra [ferret], as if from the same source. But Solomon's ב״ברא should not have been read as viverra, since viverra is a Roman word, whereas ב״ברא is purely French. [II, 493] For Rabbi Solomon was a Frenchman, and he interprets Hebrew words only by French ones. Yet from the same source the English too have here a ferret, that is, furo, an animal similar to the viverra. But it is no wonder that so many translators went astray, since they had seen neither the Syriac nor the Samaritan paraphrase, nor those two Arabic ones, from which we have extracted the true meaning of the word אנקה anaka.
